sentences.text:
Manish Vishwakarma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:21638
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal
 On The 8 th Of May, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 14614 of 2025
 Manish Vishwakarma
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ankit Saxena - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri C.M. Tiwari - Government Advocate for the respon
 No.1/State.
 Order

This is the third application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS/439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.415/2024 registered at Police Station - Bag Sevaniya,
District- Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 323, 363, 372, 373, 376, 368,
120-B, 420, 467, 468 & 471 of IPC, Section 3/4 of POCSO Act and Section 81 & 82 of Juvenile Justice Act.
Applicant is in detention since 13.07.2024.

Earlier (second) application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 19.11.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No. 48241/2024.
2.

As per the prosecution story, on 26.06.2024 co-accused accused Najma, Sunita, Sangeeta and Sunita's husband and her another friend had sold the minor prosecutrix to co-accused Durgalal in Rajasthan whereupon he committed rape with her.
It is further stated that the applicant prepared the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21638 2 MCRC-14614-2025 fake Aadhar card of the minor prosecutrix.

It is also alleged that on 13.07.2024, the forged Aadhar Card of the prosecutrix and the friend of the prosecutrix were seized from the possession of co-accused Sangeeta and above forged Aadhar card is stated to have been made by the applicant/accused.
It is alleged by the prosecution that applicant prepared the forged Aadhar Card of the prosecutrix showing her major.
Mobile and laptop were seized from the applicant.

On the basis of which, offence has been registered against the applicant and other co-accused persons under the aforesaid sections and after investigation charge-sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The applicant is in jail since 13.07.2024.
It is submitted that after rejection of earlier bail application, the Trial Court has framed the charges against present applicant only under Section 467 & 468 of IPC.
Charge under Section 120-B & 471 of IPC are not made out against present applicant.
It is further submitted that present applicant is not the main accused and no allegation regarding rape is made against present applicant.
He has no role in abducting or selling the prosecutrix.
There is also no allegation regarding conspiracy.
It is further submitted that Aadhar Card and mark sheet does not come under the category of 'valuable security'.

In this regard, learned counsel has placed reliance on the decision of Coordinate Bench of this Court in Ghanshyam Patel @
Lallu vs. State of M.P. passed in CRR. No.3829/2018.

sentences.text: Charge sheet has been filed.
The conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21638 3 MCRC-14614-2025 4.
On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and prayed for it's rejection.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.

Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S./439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant,
stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE mohsin Manish Vishwakarma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79792128/
